_meta.indication: AUBAGIO is indicated for the treatment of patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis.

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, multinational, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group study; patients randomized 1:1:1 to placebo, teriflunomide 7 mg, or teriflunomide 14 mg daily for approximately 2 years.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis (relapsing-remitting, secondary progressive)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Annualized relapse rate (ARR), defined as the number of confirmed relapses per patient-year
pivotal_trials.result: Adjusted ARR 0.539 (placebo), 0.370 (7 mg), 0.369 (14 mg); relative risk reduction 31.2% (p=0.0002) for 7 mg and 31.5% (p=0.0005) for 14 mg. Disability progression sustained for 12 weeks was significantly reduced only in the 14 mg group (20.2% vs 27.3% placebo, p=0.028, hazard ratio 0.70); 7 mg not significant (21.7%, p=0.084, hazard ratio 0.76).

nct_ctgov.title: Study of Teriflunomide in Reducing the Frequency of Relapses and Accumulation of Disability in Patients With Multiple Sclerosis

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (14 mg vs placebo) included headache (19% vs 18%), diarrhea (18% vs 9%), ALT increased (14% vs 7%), nausea (14% vs 7%), and alopecia/hair thinning (13% vs 3%). Most serious risks are hepatotoxicity and teratogenicity (boxed warning).
target_moa: Teriflunomide is an immunomodulator that selectively and reversibly inhibits the mitochondrial enzyme dihydroorotate dehydrogenase (DHO-DH), required for de novo pyrimidine synthesis, producing a cytostatic effect on proliferating T- and B-cells.

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: HEPATOTOXICITY and RISK OF TERATOGENICITY — severe liver injury including fatal liver failure has been reported with leflunomide and a similar risk is expected for teriflunomide; AUBAGIO may cause major birth defects and is contraindicated in pregnant women or women of childbearing potential not using reliable contraception.

rems.type: The sponsor submitted a REMS proposal, but FDA determined a REMS was not necessary to ensure the benefits outweigh the risks; risk mitigation was addressed through prescriber and patient labeling.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held (N/A).

description.text: Labeling update to reflect results of additional studies (TOWER and TOPIC) for teriflunomide (Aubagio)

citations.quote: This “Prior Approval” supplemental new drug application proposes an update of the teriflunomide package insert to reflect the results of additional studies including Study EFC10531/TOWER and Study EFC6260/TOPIC.
